message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"9.21","text":"For just as the soldiers subordinate to one of Caesar’s commanders of a thousand know, because of the authority of the one who granted it, to honor the person who received it—so fully that those set over them can say to one, “Come,” and he comes, and to another, “Go,” and he goes—so also the person who has given himself to God—faithful as he is—merely speaks to demons and afflictions and is obeyed; and demons withdraw, though they are much stronger than those commanding them. For by an inexpressible power God subjects each person’s mind to whomever he wishes. For just as many governors, together with all their camps and cities, have feared Caesar, although he is a man, while each person’s heart hastens to give precedence to the image of all things (for all things, enslaved by God’s will, do not know the cause because of fear), so all the spirits that produce affliction honor and flee the person who takes refuge in God and carries righteous faith in his own heart as though it were God’s image, having become afraid through some natural way.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"Καίσαρος χιλιάρχῳ","chosen":"one of Caesar’s commanders of a thousand","rationale":"χιλίαρχος literally denotes a commander of a thousand; the expanded rendering translates the office rather than merely transliterating it."},{"source_quote":"τοὺς ἐφεστῶτας","chosen":"those set over them","rationale":"The participle can denote people placed in authority; “those standing by” is also lexically possible, but the command structure favors the former."},{"source_quote":"ἀφράστῳ γὰρ δυνάμει τὸν ἑκάστου νοῦν ὁ θεὸς ὑποτάσσει ᾧ βούλεται","chosen":"For by an inexpressible power God subjects each person’s mind to whomever he wishes","rationale":"The dative relative ᾧ is taken personally as “whomever”; “to whatever he wishes” remains grammatically possible but fits the comparison with delegated personal authority less well."},{"source_quote":"τὴν τῶν ὅλων εἰκόνα","chosen":"the image of all things","rationale":"The referent of the image is not explicitly identified. The genitive may also be represented as “of the whole” or “of the universe,” so the translation does not identify the image specifically with Caesar or with God."},{"source_quote":"θεοῦ γὰρ βουλῇ τὰ πάντα δεδουλωμένα φόβῳ τὴν αἰτίαν οὐκ οἶδεν","chosen":"for all things, enslaved by God’s will, do not know the cause because of fear","rationale":"θεοῦ βουλῇ is taken instrumentally with δεδουλωμένα and φόβῳ causally with οὐκ οἶδεν. Alternatively, φόβῳ could mean that all things are “enslaved to fear.”"},{"source_quote":"τὰ παθοποιὰ πνεύματα","chosen":"the spirits that produce affliction","rationale":"πάθος can denote suffering, illness, or passion. “Affliction” retains a range broad enough for the surrounding healing and demonic context."},{"source_quote":"ὥσπερ εἰκόνα αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ αὐτοῦ βαστάζοντα καρδίᾳ","chosen":"carries righteous faith in his own heart as though it were God’s image","rationale":"The first αὐτοῦ is understood as referring to God and the second reflexively to the person taking refuge in God; the Greek itself uses the same pronoun for both."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"(πιστὸς ὢν δαίμοσίν τε καὶ πάθεσιν) μόνον λέγων ἀκούεται","issue":"The printed parentheses group δαίμοσίν τε καὶ πάθεσιν with πιστός, which could yield the contextually difficult sense “faithful/trustworthy to demons and afflictions.” The translation instead construes those datives with λέγων across the editorial parenthesis: the faithful person speaks to demons and afflictions and is obeyed. Another possible reading is that he is recognized as trustworthy by them.","proposed_reading":"πιστὸς ὢν, δαίμοσίν τε καὶ πάθεσιν μόνον λέγων, ἀκούεται","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"9.22","text":"But nevertheless, even if all demons together with all afflictions flee from you, you must not rejoice in this alone, but in the fact that, because you have proved pleasing, your names have been inscribed in heaven as those of people who live forever. Thus the divine Holy Spirit too rejoices because a human being has conquered death; for the expulsion of demons takes place for someone else’s healing. We say these things, however, not as people who deny the claim that there is no need to help others, but because one must not grow conceited over this and neglect oneself. Sometimes demons flee some lawless men because of an honored name, and both the one who drove them away and the one who witnessed what happened are ambushed. The one who drove them away is ambushed as though he had been favored because of righteousness, not knowing the demon’s villainy (for the demon has both honored the name and, by its flight, wrapped the impious man in a conceit of righteousness and deceived him into not reorienting); but the one who witnessed what happened, having associated with the one who drove them away as with a devout man and having hastened toward the same way of life, perishes. At times they also pretend to flee oaths not connected with God, so that, after deceiving them, they may destroy them whenever they wish.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"δι᾽ εὐαρεστίαν","chosen":"because you have proved pleasing","rationale":"εὐαρεστία denotes being pleasing or acceptable. God is the likely implied evaluator, but the Greek does not state the referent explicitly."},{"source_quote":"τὸ θεῖον ἅγιον πνεῦμα","chosen":"the divine Holy Spirit","rationale":"The article and paired adjectives present the spirit as the divine holy spirit in view; capitalization reflects the personal theological referent without adding a title absent from the wording."},{"source_quote":"ὁ ἱστορήσας","chosen":"the one who witnessed what happened","rationale":"ἱστορέω can mean to observe, investigate, inquire about, visit, or recount. Here it denotes the person who learns of or observes the expulsion and consequently treats the exorcist as devout."},{"source_quote":"εἰς οἴησιν δικαιοσύνης περιβαλὼν","chosen":"wrapped the impious man in a conceit of righteousness","rationale":"The rendering preserves the clothing or enveloping image of περιβάλλω; οἴησις may mean an opinion, supposition, or conceited belief."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ μὴ μετανοεῖν ἠπάτησεν","chosen":"deceived him into not reorienting","rationale":"The articular infinitive expresses the outcome sought by the deception. “Reorienting” follows the supplied terminology policy; “repenting” is the traditional alternative."},{"source_quote":"τοὺς μὴ θεῷ προσκειμένους ὅρκους","chosen":"oaths not connected with God","rationale":"The participle grammatically modifies ὅρκους and describes oaths not attached or devoted to God. Context may imply “oaths used by people not devoted to God,” but those people are not explicitly named in this phrase."},{"source_quote":"ἵν’ ἀπατήσαντες αὐτοὺς ὅτε θελήσωσιν ἀνέλωσιν","chosen":"so that, after deceiving them, they may destroy them whenever they wish","rationale":"The repeated masculine pronoun is preserved without supplying an explicit antecedent. It most plausibly concerns the people relying on the oaths, though grammatically it can refer back to the masculine plural ὅρκους."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἀλλ᾽. ὅμως","issue":"The printed period separates the elided conjunction ἀλλ᾽ from ὅμως, leaving ἀλλ᾽ abruptly isolated. The translation reads the two together as “But nevertheless” while retaining both words.","proposed_reading":"ἀλλ᾽ ὅμως","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"οὐχ ὡς ἀρνούμενοι τὸ μὴ δεῖν ἄλλοις βοηθεῖν","issue":"As printed, the nested negatives mean “not as denying the claim that there is no need to help others,” and that sense is retained in the translation. It is contextually awkward because the following clause warns only against neglecting oneself, and an intrusive μή may be suspected. The surviving wording nevertheless permits a defensible literal translation.","proposed_reading":"οὐχ ὡς ἀρνούμενοι τὸ δεῖν ἄλλοις βοηθεῖν","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"9.23","text":"So then, we want you to know this too: unless someone willingly gives himself over as a servant to demons (as I said earlier), the demon has no authority against him. Therefore, having chosen to worship one God, having abstained from the “table of demons,” having embraced self-control together with benevolence and righteousness, and having been baptized with the thrice-blessed invocation for the forgiveness of sins, by devoting yourselves as much as you can toward the perfection of purity, you can, once rescued from everlasting punishment, become heirs of eternal good things. After saying this, he ordered those troubled by afflictions to come forward. And so many, having gathered together on the evidence of those who had been healed the day before, came forward. He laid his hands on them and prayed, healing them at once; then, after instructing them and the others to assemble earlier in the morning, he himself bathed, took food, and went to sleep.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἑαυτὸν δαίμοσιν δοῦλον ἐκδῴη","chosen":"gives himself over as a servant to demons","rationale":"δοῦλος is rendered “servant” under the supplied policy, while ἐκδίδωμι conveys voluntary surrender into the demons’ ownership and control."},{"source_quote":"ὡς τάχιον εἶπον","chosen":"as I said earlier","rationale":"The comparative adverb τάχιον can mean “more quickly,” but in references to prior speech it naturally means “earlier” or “a little while ago.”"},{"source_quote":"σωφροσύνην μετὰ φιλανθρωπίας καὶ δικαιοσύνης","chosen":"self-control together with benevolence and righteousness","rationale":"σωφροσύνη can include sound-minded restraint, temperance, or chastity; φιλανθρωπία denotes humane love or benevolence; δικαιοσύνη can also be rendered “justice.”"},{"source_quote":"τρισμακαρίᾳ ἐπονομασίᾳ","chosen":"the thrice-blessed invocation","rationale":"ἐπονομασία can denote an invocation, naming, or appellation. “Invocation” fits baptismal use, but the Greek does not spell out the invoked wording."},{"source_quote":"τῷ ὅσον δύνασθε ἐπὶ τὸ τέλειον τῆς ἁγνείας ἑαυτοὺς ἐπιδιδόναι","chosen":"by devoting yourselves as much as you can toward the perfection of purity","rationale":"The articular infinitive is taken instrumentally with δύνασθε. ἁγνεία may denote purity generally or chastity specifically."},{"source_quote":"κολάσεως αἰδίου ῥυσθέντες αἰωνίων ἀγαθῶν κληρονόμοι","chosen":"once rescued from everlasting punishment, become heirs of eternal good things","rationale":"Different English terms preserve the source’s distinction between ἀΐδιος, “everlasting,” and αἰώνιος, “eternal,” without asserting that the author intended sharply different durations."},{"source_quote":"πείρᾳ τῶν ἐχθὲς θεραπευθέντων","chosen":"on the evidence of those who had been healed the day before","rationale":"πείρᾳ can refer to experience, proof, or the evidentiary effect of what was experienced; the healed people supplied the reason others gathered."},{"source_quote":"ὀρθριαίτερον συνεδρεύειν","chosen":"to assemble earlier in the morning","rationale":"ὀρθριαίτερον is a comparative referring to an earlier morning hour, while συνεδρεύω literally means to sit together and can denote meeting or assembling."}],"source_issues":[]}]}
